extracted.intended_audience: novelists and authors preparing manuscript submissions to traditional/digital-first publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklist for authors preparing and sending full-novel manuscript submissions to a digital-first commercial-fiction publisher (fits, readiness, and procedural checks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure your manuscript matches the genres the publisher is currently open to (Crime & Thriller; Historical; Romance — spicy, romantic suspense, romantic comedy, erotica; Contemporary; YA/Crossover/Adult Fantasy; Romantasy; Horror).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can get a feel for what they’ve published in the past by going to their main page and learn more about their editors; only submit into the genres they list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit with publisher focus (commercial fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm your book fits the publisher's stated focus: they focus on publishing commercial fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors whose work is not commercial fiction should not expect a good fit; researching the publisher's catalogue helps verify fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript revision completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you revised your manuscript at least three times? (The submission form asks: 'Have you revised your manuscript at least 3 times?')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site links to resources on revising; this is presented as a minimum readiness standard before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beta-reader feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you gotten beta reader feedback? (The submission form explicitly asks this.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Getting external reader feedback is treated as an important step in preparing a manuscript for submission; the site links to resources on the importance of beta readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study publisher guidelines and catalog before submitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Agree to only submit after carefully studying the publisher's guidelines and catalog (the form requires explicit agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page directs readers to the publisher's submittable page for full submission guidelines and emphasizes following those rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polish and appropriateness of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit un-polished or inappropriate work: 'Submitting to un-polished or innapropriate work can ruin your reptuation and can (and has) cause a publisher to close submissions to everyone.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a reputational and community-level risk; authors should ensure professionalism and appropriate material before sending submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check actual open/closed status and submission caps
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify the publisher's current submission status and any submission caps (the post notes the imprint reached its submission cap by the 15th and that the site did not clearly indicate closure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the submittable page showed ambiguous information (year not updated, cap reached but still accepting form submissions), authors should confirm status on the publisher's submission portal rather than relying solely on the listing page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm geographic/eligibility restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether the publisher has any geographic or other eligibility limitations (the post notes One More Chapter did not mention geographic limitations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you only want to work with publishers who will only accept authors from certain territories, confirm that explicitly; absence of mention does not always guarantee no restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand 'digital-first' publishing implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify what the publisher means by 'digital-first'—whether print publication is guaranteed, contingent on sales, or print-on-demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'digital-first' has been used to mean different things (e.g., print only if a certain number of copies sold, guaranteed print via POD, etc.); confirm print/format expectations if you require a print edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use publisher's submission portal for full requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the publisher's submittable page for full submission guidelines (the article explicitly links to that page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog post is a summary; the authoritative technical and procedural requirements (file format, word counts, synopsis, sample chapters, contact details) will be on the publisher's submission portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research publisher's past publications and editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Research the publisher's catalog and editors to judge fit: 'You can get a feel for what they’ve published in the past by going to their main page. You can learn more about their editors here.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use past titles and editor information to tailor your submission and ensure your book aligns with their editorial taste and list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider broader submission-readiness resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting, consider reading the site's broader resources (guide to 291+ manuscript publishers; articles on revising, beta readers, and appropriate submission practices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site recommends using its guides and lectures (e.g., 'Read about revising your manuscript', 'Learn more about the importance of beta readers') as part of being submission-ready.
